data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 asserts a causal mechanism (additive error-correction via redundant verification) but never answers the required evidentiary test: it fails to identify what evidence within a single evaluation would distinguish a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that merely tracks the right answer. The mechanism explains why errors are reduced when items are verified, but it provides no diagnostic signal for distinguishing cases where the panel arrives at the correct outcome through genuine verification versus through surface-level checklist completion that coincides with the right answer. Without this, the argument cannot defend its reliability claim against the counterhypothesis that the panel is merely compliant.
